baseline:
B
A Transformer block is composed of two primary sub-layers: a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a position-wise feed-forward network, which is a type of Multilayer Perceptron (MLP).

B
A multilayer perceptron (MLP) is characterized by having at least one hidden layer of neurons between its input and output layers. Crucially, these hidden neurons use non-linear activation functions, which enable the network to learn and approximate complex, non-linear relationships in data.

B
The MLP (Feed-Forward Network) processes the output of the attention layer, which are context-aware embeddings. It applies a non-linear transformation to each token's representation, allowing the model to learn more complex features and relationships from the information gathered by the attention mechanism.

C
The weights within the MLP layers are trained to recognize specific input patterns and transform them into corresponding output patterns. This effectively creates a learned key-value system where knowledge is stored as associations encoded in the network's parameters.

C
The weights (W) and biases (b) are the parameters of the network that are adjusted during the training process. This tuning process encodes the learned patterns and information (the "facts") from the training data directly into the numerical values of W and b.
